## Analysis Overview

This document imports and reshapes coding-study data, quantifies inter-coder agreement, models agreement and coding time, and produces diagnostic and presentation figures. Code statements from the source file are preserved; organizational prose, chunk labels, and comments have been added for maintainability.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Set global chunk behavior and attach analysis dependencies.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Create the figure output directory when it does not already exist.
dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(jaccard)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(scales)
library(viridis)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)
library(performance)
library(emmeans)
library(patchwork)
library(brms)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)

# Colorado State University brand colors used for AI-condition plots
csu_ai_colors <- c(
  "FALSE" = "#1E4D2B", # Colorado State Green: manual coding
  "TRUE"  = "#D9782D" # Aggie Orange: AI-assisted coding
)
# Three-level CSU palette
csu_palette_3 <- c(
  "#1E4D2B", # Colorado State Green
  "#D9782D", # Aggie Orange
  "#C8C372" # Colorado State Gold
)
# Four-level CSU Energy palette
csu_palette_4 <- c(
  "#82C503", # Lovers Lane
  "#E56A54", # Flower Trial Red
  "#7E5475", # Powered Purple
  "#008FB3" # Horsetooth Blue
)
```

## 1. Data Engineering

### 1.1 Import Data

Imports the coding records, reports their structure, removes unused columns, and retains complete coder observations.

```{r import-records}
# Read, inspect, reduce, and completeness-filter the primary record-level dataset.
# 1) Import the CSV
raw_data <- readr::read_csv("../data_entry/records_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2) Print a summary including column dtypes and total number of rows
cat("=== DataFrame Summary ===\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(raw_data), "\n")
cat("Total columns:", ncol(raw_data), "\n\n")

# Column dtypes + preview (built-in tidyverse helper)
dplyr::glimpse(raw_data)

# 3) Drop specified columns
records_df <- raw_data %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("diagnosis", "assessment", "pathology")))

# 4) Filter for rows with non-empty values in ALL listed columns
required_cols <- c("nadia", "katie", "terri", "beth", "naija", "erik", "caitlin", "tracy")

records_df <- records_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_all(
      dplyr::all_of(required_cols),
      ~ !is.na(.) &
        stringr::str_trim(as.character(.)) != "" &
        stringr::str_trim(as.character(.)) != "nan"
    )
  )

# 5) Report the updated row count
cat("\n=== After Dropping Columns + Filtering ===\n")
cat("Updated rows:", nrow(records_df), "\n")

# 6) Print the head of the dataframe
cat("\n=== Head of DataFrame ===\n")
print(head(records_df))
```

### 1.2 Reference Code Dictionary

Imports and cleans the master list of allowable codes used as the one-hot encoding reference.

```{r import-reference-codes}
# Build a stable numeric reference vector from the external code dictionary.
# Import reference codes
all_codes_df <- readr::read_csv("all_codes.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

# Pull first column as the reference list (works whether the column is named or not)
all_codes <- all_codes_df %>%
  dplyr::pull(1) %>%
  stringr::str_trim() %>%
  .[. != "" & !is.na(.)] %>%
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric()) %>% # convert valid code strings to numeric values
  .[!is.na(.)] %>% # remove entries that could not be parsed as codes
  unique()

# Optional: keep reference codes in a stable order
all_codes <- sort(all_codes)

cat("Number of Codes:", length(all_codes), "\n")
```

### 1.3 Data Reshaping

Reshapes coder-specific columns into one row per record and coder, then assigns each coder to an experience group.

```{r reshape-records-long}
# Standardize coder columns before pivoting them to a tidy long representation.
subjects <- c("nadia", "katie", "terri", "beth", "naija", "erik", "caitlin", "tracy")

records_long <- records_df %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0("codes_", .x), .cols = any_of(subjects)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(codes|time|order)_"),
    names_to = c(".value", "coder"),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      coder %in% c("nadia", "katie", "tracy") ~ "clinicians",
      coder %in% c("terri", "beth") ~ "coders",
      coder %in% c("naija", "erik", "caitlin") ~ "students",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(record_id, ai, coder, group, codes, time, order) %>%
  arrange(record_id, match(coder, subjects))
```

### 1.4 Feature Engineering

Calculates character length from diagnosis and assessment text as a record-level covariate. Adds the record-level text-length covariate to the long-format coding data.

```{r record-text-length}
# Use source text from raw_data because diagnosis and assessment were removed from records_df.
record_lens <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(
    combined_text = paste(diagnosis, assessment, sep = " "),
    text_length   = nchar(combined_text)
  ) %>%
  select(c(record_id, text_length))

# Join the record-level covariate while retaining the current row order and all coder observations.
records_long <- records_long %>%
  dplyr::left_join(record_lens, by = "record_id")

head(records_long)
```

Defines helpers for pairwise Jaccard similarity and the mean similarity across all coder pairs.

```{r define-jaccard-functions}
# Keep similarity calculations in reusable helpers so the grouped analysis remains readable.
# Function to calculate pairwise Jaccard score
jaccard_pairwise <- function(rater1, rater2) {
  return(jaccard::jaccard(rater1, rater2))
}

# Helper: average of all pairwise jaccards in a list of one-hot vectors
avg_pairwise_jaccard <- function(onehot_list) {
  # keep only non-null vectors
  onehot_list <- onehot_list[!vapply(onehot_list, is.null, logical(1))]

  n <- length(onehot_list)
  if (n < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  pairs <- combn(n, 2)

  scores <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_len(ncol(pairs)), function(k) {
    v1 <- onehot_list[[pairs[1, k]]]
    v2 <- onehot_list[[pairs[2, k]]]
    s <- jaccard_pairwise(v1, v2)

    # If both vectors are all-zeros, some implementations return NaN (0/0).
    # Common convention for Jaccard(empty, empty) is 1. Adjust if you prefer 0.
    if (is.nan(s)) {
      s <- 1
    }
    s
  })

  mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

Defines a parser that converts newline-separated code strings into unique numeric code vectors.

```{r define-code-parser}
# Normalize stored code text before it is encoded for agreement calculations.
# Convert newline-separated code text into a numeric vector
codes_text_to_numeric <- function(x, unique_codes = TRUE) {
  # Treat NA as empty
  if (is.na(x)) {
    return(numeric(0))
  }

  # Coerce to character in case a factor slips in
  x <- as.character(x)

  # Trim overall string; if empty after trim, return empty vector
  x_trim <- stringr::str_trim(x)
  if (identical(x_trim, "") ||
    nchar(x_trim) == 0) {
    return(numeric(0))
  }

  # Split on any line break (\n, \r\n, \r)
  parts <- stringr::str_split(x_trim, pattern = "\\r?\\n|\\r")[[1]]

  # Trim each element and drop empties
  parts <- stringr::str_trim(parts)
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  if (length(parts) == 0) {
    return(numeric(0))
  }

  # Convert to numeric
  nums <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(parts))

  # Drop any non-numeric entries (if present)
  nums <- nums[!is.na(nums)]

  if (unique_codes) {
    nums <- unique(nums)
  }

  nums
}
```

Defines a helper that maps each code vector to a binary vector aligned with the reference code list.

```{r define-one-hot-encoder}
# Encode observed codes against all_codes so every coder vector has identical length and order.
# One-hot encode a numeric code vector against the all_codes reference list
one_hot_encode_codes <- function(codes_vec, ref_codes = all_codes) {
  # Handle NULL / NA / empty
  if (is.null(codes_vec) ||
    length(codes_vec) == 0 || all(is.na(codes_vec))) {
    out <- integer(length(ref_codes))
    names(out) <- as.character(ref_codes)
    return(out)
  }

  # Ensure numeric + unique to avoid redundant indexing
  codes_vec <- unique(as.numeric(codes_vec))
  codes_vec <- codes_vec[!is.na(codes_vec)]

  out <- integer(length(ref_codes))
  names(out) <- as.character(ref_codes)

  # Efficient set membership via match (faster than %in% for large vectors)
  idx <- match(codes_vec, ref_codes, nomatch = 0L)
  idx <- idx[idx > 0L]
  if (length(idx) > 0L) {
    out[idx] <- 1L
  }

  out
}
```

Calculates average pairwise Jaccard agreement for every record and coder group, including missing record-group combinations.

```{r calculate-group-jaccard}
# Create a complete record-by-group agreement table for modeling and plotting.
# Define the groups you expect (so we can guarantee one row per record/group)
group_levels <- c("clinicians", "coders", "students")

# Compute avg pairwise jaccard per record/group
ai_by_record <- records_long %>%
  distinct(record_id, ai)

jaccard_by_record_group <- records_long %>%
  mutate(
    codes_vec = purrr::map(codes, codes_text_to_numeric),
    onehot    = purrr::map(codes_vec, one_hot_encode_codes, ref_codes = all_codes)
  ) %>%
  group_by(record_id, group) %>%
  summarise(
    ai = first(ai),
    # ai is constant within record
    jaccard_avg = avg_pairwise_jaccard(onehot),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # ensure one row per group per record_id
  right_join(
    tidyr::expand_grid(record_id = sort(unique(
      records_long$record_id
    )), group = group_levels),
    by = c("record_id", "group")
  ) %>%
  left_join(ai_by_record, by = "record_id", suffix = c("", ".ref")) %>%
  mutate(
    ai = coalesce(ai, ai.ref),
    group = factor(group, levels = group_levels)
  ) %>%
  select(record_id, ai, group, jaccard_avg) %>%
  arrange(record_id, group)
```

Adds record text length to the record-by-group Jaccard analysis table.

```{r join-jaccard-text-length}
# Join the text-length adjustment variable while retaining all rows in the Jaccard outcome table.
jaccard_by_record_group <- jaccard_by_record_group %>%
  dplyr::left_join(record_lens, by = "record_id")

jaccard_by_record_group
```

Creates a coder-specific global task-order variable for the coding-time model.

```{r create-global-task-order}
# Construct sequential task order within coder for use as a fixed effect.
records_long <- records_long %>%
  group_by(coder) %>%
  arrange(order, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(order_global = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()
```

### 2.2 AI Suggestion Acceptance

```{r ai-suggestion-acceptance}
# The uploaded source referenced ai_comparison without creating it. Construct it from
# raw_data when the required columns are present; otherwise skip only this optional
# overlap summary so the full document remains executable from a clean R session.
ai_comparison <- if (all(c("response_codes", "predicted_codes", "group") %in% names(raw_data))) {
  raw_data %>%
    transmute(
      response_codes = purrr::map(response_codes, codes_text_to_numeric),
      predicted_codes = purrr::map(predicted_codes, codes_text_to_numeric),
      group = as.character(group)
    )
} else {
  NULL
}

if (is.null(ai_comparison)) {
  overlap_summary <- tibble::tibble(
    Note = paste(
      "AI suggestion-acceptance analysis was not run because raw_data does not",
      "contain response_codes, predicted_codes, and group columns."
    )
  )
  overlap_summary
} else {
  ai_overlap_table <- ai_comparison %>%
    mutate(
      response_codes = map(response_codes, unique),
      predicted_codes = map(predicted_codes, unique),
      n_submitted = map_int(response_codes, length),
      n_suggested = map_int(predicted_codes, length),
      n_overlap = map2_int(
        response_codes,
        predicted_codes,
        ~ length(intersect(.x, .y))
      ),
      n_added = n_submitted - n_overlap,
      n_omitted = n_suggested - n_overlap,
      any_added = n_added > 0,
      any_omitted = n_omitted > 0,
      exact_match = map2_lgl(
        response_codes,
        predicted_codes,
        ~ setequal(.x, .y)
      )
    )

  summarise_overlap <- function(data) {
    tibble(
      `Submitted-code overlap` =
        sum(data$n_overlap) / sum(data$n_submitted),
      `Suggestion acceptance` =
        sum(data$n_overlap) / sum(data$n_suggested),
      `Added-code rate` =
        sum(data$n_added) / sum(data$n_submitted),
      `Responses with >=1 added code` =
        mean(data$any_added),
      `Responses with >=1 omitted suggestion` =
        mean(data$any_omitted),
      `Exact-set match` =
        mean(data$exact_match)
    ) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        everything(),
        names_to = "measure",
        values_to = "proportion"
      )
  }

  overall_overlap <- summarise_overlap(ai_overlap_table) %>%
    mutate(group = "Overall")

  group_overlap <- ai_overlap_table %>%
    group_split(group) %>%
    map_dfr(
      ~ summarise_overlap(.x) %>%
        mutate(group = as.character(first(.x$group)))
    )

  overlap_summary <- bind_rows(
    overall_overlap,
    group_overlap
  ) %>%
    mutate(percentage = 100 * proportion) %>%
    select(measure, group, percentage) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = group,
      values_from = percentage
    ) %>%
    rename(
      Measure = measure,
      Clinicians = clinicians,
      Coders = coders,
      Students = students
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, digits = 1))

  overlap_summary
}
```

### 2.3 Exploratory Plots

Creates and saves faceted histograms of record-level Jaccard agreement by AI use and coder group.

```{r plot-jaccard-distribution}
# Prepare display labels, facet summaries, and the final agreement histogram.
jaccard_hist_df <- jaccard_by_record_group %>%
  rename(`AI Use` = ai, Group = group) %>%
  mutate(
    `AI Use` = case_when(
      `AI Use` == TRUE ~ "AI-Assisted Coding",
      `AI Use` == FALSE ~ "Manual Coding",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Group = toupper(Group),
    # Nice ordering & stable legend
    `AI Use` = factor(`AI Use`, levels = c("Manual Coding", "AI-Assisted Coding"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`AI Use`), !is.na(Group), !is.na(jaccard_avg))

jaccard_vline_df <- jaccard_hist_df %>%
  group_by(`AI Use`) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_jaccard = mean(jaccard_avg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_jaccard_hist <- ggplot(jaccard_hist_df, aes(x = jaccard_avg, fill = Group)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.05,
    boundary = 0,
    closed = "left",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = jaccard_vline_df,
    aes(xintercept = mean_jaccard),
    color = "black",
    linetype = "22",
    # clean dashed
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = jaccard_vline_df,
    aes(
      x = mean_jaccard,
      y = Inf,
      label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean_jaccard, 2)),
      hjust = ifelse(mean_jaccard > 0.8, 1.1, -0.1) # shift left if near 1
    ),
    vjust = 1.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  facet_grid(`AI Use` ~ .) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = function(x) {
      ifelse(x %in% c(0, 1), sprintf("%.1f", x), sprintf("%.1f", x))
    }
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = csu_palette_3) +
  labs(
    # title = "Inter-Coder Reliability",
    # subtitle = "per record x group",
    # subtitle = "Faceted by AI usage; dashed line indicates mean within facet",
    x = "Jaccard Index",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0.6, "lines"),
    # small increase only
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5))
  )

p_jaccard_hist

ggsave(
  "../plots/jaccard_hist.png",
  plot = p_jaccard_hist,
  width = 8,
  height = 8,
  # <-- increase this
```

Creates and saves a faceted coding-time trend plot by AI use and coder group.

```{r plot-coding-speed}
# Re-index task order within coder and AI condition before plotting coding-time trajectories.
coding_speed_df <- records_long %>%
  group_by(coder, ai) %>%
  arrange(order, .by_group = TRUE) %>% # preserves the intended sequence
  mutate(order = row_number()) %>% # re-index within coder × ai
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(`AI Use` = ai) %>%
  mutate(
    `AI Use` = case_when(
      `AI Use` == TRUE ~ "AI-Assisted Coding",
      `AI Use` == FALSE ~ "Manual Coding",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(Group = group) %>%
  mutate(Group = toupper(Group)) %>%
  mutate(`AI Use` = factor(`AI Use`, levels = c("Manual Coding", "AI-Assisted Coding")))

coding_speed_hline_df <- coding_speed_df %>%
  group_by(`AI Use`) %>%
  summarise(mean_time = mean(time, na.rm = TRUE))

p2 <- ggplot(coding_speed_df, aes(x = order, y = time, color = Group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
```

## 3. Jaccard Agreement Models

### 3.1 Original boundary-adjusted beta model

This section retains the original Smithson-Verkuilen-style boundary-adjusted beta mixed-effects analysis unchanged so that the original results remain reproducible.

Moves Jaccard values away from exact zero and one so they can be modeled with a beta distribution.

```{r transform-jaccard-beta}
# Apply a standard boundary adjustment required for beta outcomes at 0 or 1.
n <- nrow(jaccard_by_record_group)

jaccard_by_record_group <- jaccard_by_record_group %>%
  mutate(jaccard_beta = (jaccard_avg * (n - 1) + 0.5) / n)
```

Fits a beta mixed-effects model for Jaccard agreement with AI use, group, text length, and record-level random intercepts.

```{r fit-jaccard-beta-model}
# Model agreement while accounting for repeated group observations within records.
fit_beta <- glmmTMB(
  jaccard_beta ~ ai * group + text_length + (1 | record_id),
  family = beta_family(),
  data = jaccard_by_record_group
)

summary(fit_beta)
```

#### 3.1.1 Jaccard Model Diagnostics

Evaluates the beta model with simulated residuals, residual plots, and model-fit summaries.

```{r diagnose-jaccard-model}
# Inspect residual behavior and summarize explanatory performance for the fitted beta model.
sim_beta <- simulateResiduals(fit_beta)
plot(sim_beta)

qqnorm(residuals(fit_beta))
qqline(residuals(fit_beta))

beta_residuals_df <- data.frame(
  fitted = fitted(fit_beta),
  residuals = residuals(fit_beta)
)

ggplot(beta_residuals_df, aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted") +
  theme_minimal()

performance::model_performance(fit_beta)

# R2 (comparable metric)
r2(fit_beta)
```

#### 3.1.2 Jaccard Model Inference

Calculates estimated marginal means and Tukey-adjusted pairwise contrasts for the AI-by-group interaction.

```{r estimate-jaccard-interaction}
# Estimate all AI-use and coder-group combinations on the response scale.
emm_beta <- emmeans(fit_beta, ~ ai * group, type = "response")

pairs(emm_beta, adjust = "tukey")
confint(pairs(emm_beta))
```

Prints the response-scale estimated marginal means for each AI-by-group combination.

```{r summarize-jaccard-emmeans}
# Display the interaction-level marginal mean estimates used for interpretation.
summary(emm_beta)
```

Calculates response-scale marginal means and contrasts for AI use averaged across groups.

```{r contrast-jaccard-ai}
# Test the average AI-use contrast across coder groups.
emm_beta_ai <- emmeans(fit_beta, ~ai, type = "response")
summary(emm_beta_ai)
pairs(emm_beta_ai)
confint(pairs(emm_beta_ai))
```

Calculates response-scale marginal means and contrasts for coder group averaged across AI conditions.

```{r contrast-jaccard-group}
# Test pairwise coder-group differences averaged across AI-use conditions.
emm_beta_group <- emmeans(fit_beta, ~group, type = "response")
summary(emm_beta_group)
pairs(emm_beta_group)
```

#### 3.1.3 Jaccard Model Visualization

Plots and saves predicted Jaccard agreement and confidence intervals by group and AI use.

```{r plot-jaccard-emmeans}
# Convert response-scale estimated marginal means to a plotting data frame.
# glmmTMB uses asymptotic confidence-limit names, which are standardized here
# so the plotting code does not depend on model-specific column labels.
plot_beta <- as.data.frame(summary(emm_beta, type = "response")) %>%
  transmute(
    ai,
    group = toupper(group),
    response,
    lower.CL = asymp.LCL,
    upper.CL = asymp.UCL
  )

p_jaccard_emmeans <- ggplot(
  plot_beta,
  aes(x = group, y = response, color = ai, group = ai)
) +
  # CI bars first so lines/points sit on top
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  # Optional: keep within Jaccard bounds (0–1) without chopping CIs off harshly
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 0.8), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) + # slight buffer (not 0 to avoid clipping)
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 0.8), clip = "off") +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = csu_ai_colors,
    breaks = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    labels = c(
      "Manual Coding",
      "AI-Assisted Coding"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Jaccard Agreement",
    x = "Group",
    y = "Predicted Jaccard Index",
    color = "AI Use"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5))
  )

ggsave(

  plot = p_jaccard_emmeans,
  width = 8,

  dpi = 300
```

### 3.2 Zero-one-inflated beta sensitivity analysis

This sensitivity analysis models the original, untransformed `jaccard_avg` outcome. The zero-one-inflated beta family represents three portions of the outcome distribution: an exact-zero mass, an exact-one mass, and a continuous beta distribution for values strictly between zero and one. In `brms`, `zoi` is the probability of being in either boundary mass, `coi` is the conditional probability that a boundary observation is one rather than zero, `mu` is the mean of the interior beta component, and `phi` is its precision. Therefore, the overall expected response is

\[
E(Y) = zoi \times coi + (1-zoi) \times mu.
\]

All marginal estimates below use `posterior_epred()`, which evaluates this full expected-response quantity rather than only the interior beta mean. Record-level random effects are excluded (`re_formula = NA`) to obtain population-level estimates, text length is held at its observed mean, and groups are equally weighted when an estimate is averaged across participant groups. This matches the equal-weighted reference-grid convention used by `emmeans` for the original model.

```{r prepare-zoib-data}
# Preserve the original logical AI coding and the established group reference order.
zoib_data <- jaccard_by_record_group %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(jaccard_avg),
    !is.na(ai),
    !is.na(group),
    !is.na(text_length),
    !is.na(record_id)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ai = factor(ai, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
    group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
    record_id = factor(record_id),
    text_length_c = text_length - mean(text_length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

if (any(zoib_data$jaccard_avg < 0 | zoib_data$jaccard_avg > 1)) {
  stop("The untransformed Jaccard outcome must lie in [0, 1].")
}

cat("Exact zeroes:", sum(zoib_data$jaccard_avg == 0), "\n")
cat("Exact ones:", sum(zoib_data$jaccard_avg == 1), "\n")
cat("Interior observations:", sum(zoib_data$jaccard_avg > 0 & zoib_data$jaccard_avg < 1), "\n")
```

#### 3.2.1 Model specification and priors

The population-level coefficients use Normal(0, 1.5) priors on the logit scale, with a slightly broader Normal(0, 2) prior for the intercept. The record random-intercept standard deviation uses a half-Student-t prior. Beta precision uses a Gamma(2, 0.1) prior. The zero/one inflation probability uses a Beta(1, 4) prior, which weakly regularizes the model toward boundary values being less common than interior values. The conditional probability that an inflated boundary value is one uses a uniform Beta(1, 1) prior.

```{r specify-zoib-model-priors}
zoib_formula <- bf(
  jaccard_avg ~ ai * group + text_length_c + (1 | record_id)
)

zoib_priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "b"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sd", group = "record_id"),
  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "phi"),
  prior(beta(1, 4), class = "zoi"),
  prior(beta(1, 1), class = "coi")
)

cat("Priors supplied to the zero-one-inflated beta model:\n")
print(zoib_priors)
cat("\nPrior slots available for this model and installed brms version:\n")
print(get_prior(
  formula = zoib_formula,
  data = zoib_data,
  family = zero_one_inflated_beta()
))
```

```{r fit-zoib-model, cache=TRUE}
# Use cmdstanr when it is installed and configured; otherwise use brms/rstan.
cmdstan_version <- if (requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tryCatch(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(), error = function(e) NULL)
} else {
  NULL
}
brms_backend <- if (is.null(cmdstan_version)) "rstan" else "cmdstanr"
cat("brms backend:", brms_backend, "\n")

set.seed(20261028)
fit_zoib <- brm(
  formula = zoib_formula,
  data = zoib_data,
  family = zero_one_inflated_beta(),
  prior = zoib_priors,
  backend = brms_backend,
  chains = 4,
  cores = min(4, parallel::detectCores()),
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 20261028,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.97, max_treedepth = 15),
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  refresh = 200
)
print(summary(fit_zoib))
```

#### 3.2.2 Convergence and sampling diagnostics

```{r diagnose-zoib-sampling}
zoib_draws <- posterior::as_draws(fit_zoib)
zoib_diagnostics <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  zoib_draws,
  "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
)
print(zoib_diagnostics)

nuts_zoib <- brms::nuts_params(fit_zoib)
n_divergent <- sum(
  nuts_zoib$Parameter == "divergent__" & nuts_zoib$Value == 1
)
cat("Divergent transitions:", n_divergent, "\n")
cat("Maximum R-hat:", max(zoib_diagnostics$rhat, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Minimum bulk ESS:", min(zoib_diagnostics$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Minimum tail ESS:", min(zoib_diagnostics$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

plot(fit_zoib)
```

#### 3.2.3 Posterior predictive checks

```{r zoib-posterior-predictive-checks, fig.height=6, fig.width=8}
set.seed(20261028)
yrep_zoib <- posterior_predict(fit_zoib, ndraws = 1000)
y_obs_zoib <- zoib_data$jaccard_avg

# Full outcome distribution, including the exact-zero and exact-one masses.
pp_check(fit_zoib, type = "hist", ndraws = 100) +
  labs(title = "Posterior predictive check: full Jaccard distribution")

boundary_ppc <- tibble(
  component = c("Exactly 0", "Exactly 1"),
  observed = c(mean(y_obs_zoib == 0), mean(y_obs_zoib == 1)),
  predicted_mean = c(mean(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 0)), mean(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 1))),
  predicted_lower = c(
    quantile(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 0), 0.025),
    quantile(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 1), 0.025)
  ),
  predicted_upper = c(
    quantile(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 0), 0.975),
    quantile(rowMeans(yrep_zoib == 1), 0.975)
  )
)
knitr::kable(boundary_ppc, digits = 3,
             caption = "Observed and posterior-predicted boundary proportions")

# Compare only the continuous interior after removing exact boundary values.
set.seed(20261028)
interior_draw_ids <- sort(sample(seq_len(nrow(yrep_zoib)), min(100, nrow(yrep_zoib))))
interior_ppc_df <- purrr::map_dfr(interior_draw_ids, function(i) {
  vals <- yrep_zoib[i, ]
  tibble(draw = factor(i), value = vals[vals > 0 & vals < 1])
})
interior_obs_df <- tibble(value = y_obs_zoib[y_obs_zoib > 0 & y_obs_zoib < 1])

ggplot() +
  geom_density(
    data = interior_ppc_df,
    aes(x = value, group = draw),
    color = "grey65", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_density(
    data = interior_obs_df,
    aes(x = value),
    color = "black", linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior predictive check: continuous interior",
    subtitle = "Black = observed; gray = posterior predictive draws",
    x = "Jaccard index conditional on 0 < Jaccard < 1",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

#### 3.2.4 Coefficients and full-distribution marginal estimates

```{r zoib-coefficients}
zoib_coef_draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit_zoib)
coef_names <- grep(
  "(^b_)|(^phi$)|(^zoi$)|(^coi$)",
  names(zoib_coef_draws),
  value = TRUE
)
zoib_coefficients <- purrr::map_dfr(coef_names, function(term) {
  x <- zoib_coef_draws[[term]]
  tibble(
    term = term,
    estimate = mean(x),
    lower_95 = quantile(x, 0.025),
    upper_95 = quantile(x, 0.975),
    probability_positive = mean(x > 0)
  )
})
knitr::kable(
  zoib_coefficients,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Zero-one-inflated beta model coefficients with 95% credible intervals"
)
```

```{r zoib-marginal-estimates}
# posterior_epred() returns E(Y), combining exact-zero, exact-one, and interior-beta components.
zoib_reference_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  ai = factor(c(FALSE, TRUE), levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
  group = factor(group_levels, levels = group_levels)
) %>%
  mutate(
    text_length_c = 0,
    record_id = zoib_data$record_id[1]
  )

zoib_epred_grid <- posterior_epred(
  fit_zoib,
  newdata = zoib_reference_grid,
  re_formula = NA
)

summarize_posterior <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    estimate = mean(x),
    lower_95 = quantile(x, 0.025),
    upper_95 = quantile(x, 0.975),
    probability_positive = mean(x > 0)
  )
}

zoib_group_condition <- bind_cols(
  zoib_reference_grid %>% select(ai, group),
  tibble(
    estimate = apply(zoib_epred_grid, 2, mean),
    lower_95 = apply(zoib_epred_grid, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
    upper_95 = apply(zoib_epred_grid, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
  )
)
knitr::kable(
  zoib_group_condition,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Condition-specific expected Jaccard within participant group"
)

manual_cols <- which(zoib_reference_grid$ai == FALSE)
ai_cols <- which(zoib_reference_grid$ai == TRUE)
zoib_manual_draw <- rowMeans(zoib_epred_grid[, manual_cols, drop = FALSE])
zoib_ai_draw <- rowMeans(zoib_epred_grid[, ai_cols, drop = FALSE])

zoib_condition_marginal <- bind_rows(
  summarize_posterior(zoib_manual_draw) %>% mutate(ai = factor(FALSE, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))),
  summarize_posterior(zoib_ai_draw) %>% mutate(ai = factor(TRUE, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
) %>%
  select(ai, everything())
knitr::kable(
  zoib_condition_marginal,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Condition-specific marginal expected Jaccard, equally averaged across groups"
)

zoib_overall_ai_contrast_draw <- zoib_ai_draw - zoib_manual_draw
zoib_overall_ai_contrast <- summarize_posterior(zoib_overall_ai_contrast_draw) %>%
  mutate(contrast = "AI-assisted minus manual") %>%
  select(contrast, everything())
knitr::kable(
  zoib_overall_ai_contrast,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Overall AI-assisted versus manual contrast"
)

# AI-minus-manual condition effect within each participant group.
zoib_group_contrast_draws <- sapply(seq_along(group_levels), function(g) {
  zoib_epred_grid[, ai_cols[g]] - zoib_epred_grid[, manual_cols[g]]
})
colnames(zoib_group_contrast_draws) <- group_levels
zoib_group_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(group_levels, function(g) {
  summarize_posterior(zoib_group_contrast_draws[, g]) %>% mutate(group = g)
}) %>%
  select(group, everything())
knitr::kable(
  zoib_group_contrasts,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "AI-assisted minus manual contrast within each participant group"
)

# Difference-in-differences: pairwise comparisons of the group-specific AI effects.
interaction_pairs <- combn(group_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)
zoib_interaction_contrasts <- purrr::map_dfr(interaction_pairs, function(pair) {
  draw <- zoib_group_contrast_draws[, pair[1]] - zoib_group_contrast_draws[, pair[2]]
  summarize_posterior(draw) %>%
    mutate(contrast = paste0("AI effect: ", pair[1], " minus ", pair[2]))
}) %>%
  select(contrast, everything())
knitr::kable(
  zoib_interaction_contrasts,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Condition-by-group interaction contrasts"
)
```

#### 3.2.5 Comparison with the original boundary-adjusted beta model

```{r compare-beta-and-zoib}
# Original-model estimates are retained on their response scale.
beta_group_df <- as.data.frame(summary(emm_beta, type = "response"))
beta_ai_df <- as.data.frame(summary(emm_beta_ai, type = "response"))

beta_manual <- beta_ai_df$response[as.character(beta_ai_df$ai) == "FALSE"]
beta_ai <- beta_ai_df$response[as.character(beta_ai_df$ai) == "TRUE"]

comparison_overall <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    model = "Original boundary-adjusted beta",
    manual = beta_manual,
    ai_assisted = beta_ai,
    relative_percent_change = 100 * (beta_ai - beta_manual) / beta_manual
  ),
  tibble(
    model = "Zero-one-inflated beta",
    manual = mean(zoib_manual_draw),
    ai_assisted = mean(zoib_ai_draw),
    relative_percent_change = mean(100 * (zoib_ai_draw - zoib_manual_draw) / zoib_manual_draw)
  )
)
knitr::kable(
  comparison_overall,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Overall original-model and zero-one-inflated-model estimates"
)

comparison_group <- beta_group_df %>%
  transmute(
    model = "Original boundary-adjusted beta",
    group = as.character(group),
    condition = if_else(as.character(ai) == "TRUE", "AI-assisted", "Manual"),
    estimate = response
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(
    zoib_group_condition %>%
      transmute(
        model = "Zero-one-inflated beta",
        group = as.character(group),
        condition = if_else(as.character(ai) == "TRUE", "AI-assisted", "Manual"),
        estimate
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(group, condition, model)
knitr::kable(
  comparison_group,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Group-specific manual and AI-assisted estimates by model"
)
```

#### 3.2.6 Automatically generated sensitivity interpretation

```{r interpret-zoib-sensitivity, results='asis'}
beta_ai_difference <- beta_ai - beta_manual
zoib_ai_difference <- mean(zoib_overall_ai_contrast_draw)
zoib_ai_ci <- quantile(zoib_overall_ai_contrast_draw, c(0.025, 0.975))
zoib_prob_positive <- mean(zoib_overall_ai_contrast_draw > 0)

direction_changed <- sign(beta_ai_difference) != sign(zoib_ai_difference)
absolute_change <- abs(zoib_ai_difference - beta_ai_difference)
relative_magnitude_change <- if (abs(beta_ai_difference) > .Machine$double.eps) {
  abs(zoib_ai_difference / beta_ai_difference - 1)
} else {
  Inf
}

# Predeclared rule: material change = direction reversal, >=0.05 absolute Jaccard
# difference, or >=25% change in the estimated AI-effect magnitude.
material_change <- direction_changed || absolute_change >= 0.05 || relative_magnitude_change >= 0.25

interpretation_text <- paste0(
  "The zero-one-inflated beta sensitivity analysis estimated an overall AI-assisted minus manual difference of ",
  sprintf("%.3f", zoib_ai_difference),
  " (95% credible interval ", sprintf("%.3f", zoib_ai_ci[1]), " to ",
  sprintf("%.3f", zoib_ai_ci[2]), "; posterior probability of a positive AI effect = ",
  sprintf("%.3f", zoib_prob_positive), "). The original boundary-adjusted beta model estimated a difference of ",
  sprintf("%.3f", beta_ai_difference), ". Under the prespecified comparison rule (direction reversal, an absolute change of at least 0.05 Jaccard units, or at least a 25% change in effect magnitude), the sensitivity analysis ",
  ifelse(material_change, "materially changes", "does not materially change"),
  " the direction or magnitude of the primary AI-assistance finding."
)
cat(interpretation_text)
```

## 4. Coding Time Model

Fits a linear mixed-effects model for log coding time with coder and record random intercepts.

```{r fit-time-lmm}
# Model log-transformed duration while accounting for repeated observations by coder and record.
# Log transformation requires every modeled coding-time value to be strictly positive.
if (any(records_long$time <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  stop("Coding time contains zero or negative values and cannot be log-transformed.")
}

fit_time <- lmer(
  log(time) ~ ai * group + order_global + text_length +
    (1 | coder) + (1 | record_id),
  data = records_long,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(fit_time)
anova(fit_time, type = 3)
```

### 5.1 Coding Time Model Diagnostics

Evaluates the coding-time model with residual diagnostics and model-fit summaries.

```{r diagnose-time-model}
# Inspect duration-model residuals
sim_time <- simulateResiduals(fit_time)
plot(sim_time)

qqnorm(residuals(fit_time))
qqline(residuals(fit_time))

time_residuals_df <- data.frame(
  fitted = fitted(fit_time),
  residuals = residuals(fit_time)
)

ggplot(time_residuals_df, aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted") +
  theme_minimal()

performance::model_performance(fit_time)

# R2 (comparable metric)
r2(fit_time)
```

### 5.2 Coding Time Model Inference

Calculates response-scale estimated marginal means and Tukey-adjusted contrasts for the time-model interaction.

```{r estimate-time-interaction}
# Estimate interaction-level coding times and multiplicity-adjusted contrasts.
emm_time <- emmeans(fit_time, ~ ai * group, type = "response")
pairs(emm_time, adjust = "tukey")
confint(pairs(emm_time))
```

Prints the response-scale estimated marginal means from the coding-time model.

```{r summarize-time-emmeans}
# Display the interaction-level time estimates used for interpretation.
summary(emm_time)
```

Calculates response-scale marginal means and contrasts for AI use in the coding-time model.

```{r contrast-time-ai}
# Test the average AI-use contrast for coding time.
emm_time_ai <- emmeans(fit_time, ~ai, type = "response")
summary(emm_time_ai)
pairs(emm_time_ai)
confint(pairs(emm_time_ai))
```

### 5.3 Coding-Time Model Visualization

Plots and saves predicted coding time and confidence intervals by group and AI use.

```{r plot-time-emmeans}
# Convert response-scale estimated marginal means to a plotting data frame.
# lmer confidence limits are retained under standardized names for consistency
# with the Jaccard prediction data used in the combined figure.
# Request response-scale estimates and confidence intervals explicitly.
plot_time <- as.data.frame(
  confint(emm_time, type = "response")
)

# Identify the confidence-limit names returned by the installed emmeans
# version and the degrees-of-freedom method used for this model.
lower_ci_col <- intersect(
  c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"),
  names(plot_time)
)

upper_ci_col <- intersect(
  c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"),
  names(plot_time)
)

# Stop with an informative error if confidence limits are unavailable.
if (length(lower_ci_col) == 0 || length(upper_ci_col) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Confidence-limit columns were not found. Available columns are: ",
    paste(names(plot_time), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Standardize the confidence-limit names for downstream plotting.
plot_time <- plot_time %>%
  transmute(
    ai,
    group = toupper(group),
    response,
    lower.CL = .data[[lower_ci_col[1]]],
    upper.CL = .data[[upper_ci_col[1]]]
  )

p_time_emmeans <- ggplot(
  plot_time,
  aes(x = group, y = response, color = ai, group = ai)
) +
  # CI bars first so lines/points sit on top
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  # Optional: keep within Jaccard bounds (0–1) without chopping CIs off harshly
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 0.8), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) + # slight buffer (not 0 to avoid clipping)
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 0.8), clip = "off") +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)) +
  # scale_y_continuous(
  #   # breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
  #   labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
  # ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = csu_ai_colors,
    breaks = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    labels = c(
      "Manual Coding",
      "AI-Assisted Coding"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Coding Time",
    x = "Group",
    y = "Estimated Geometric Mean Time [seconds]",
    color = "AI Use"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5))
  )

p_time_emmeans

ggsave(
  "../plots/time_emmeans.png",
  plot = p_time_emmeans,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## 5. Misc Plots for Poster

Recreates the Jaccard and time prediction panels and saves them as a combined figure with a shared legend.

```{r combine-model-plots}
# Assemble publication-style model panels
# --- Plot 1: Jaccard ---
p_beta <- ggplot(
  plot_beta,
  aes(x = group, y = response, color = ai, group = ai)
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.15)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 0.8), clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = csu_ai_colors,
    breaks = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    labels = c(
      "Manual Coding",
      "AI-Assisted Coding"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Jaccard\nAgreement",
    x = "Group",
    y = "Predicted Jaccard Index",
    color = "AI Use"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 5, 12, 10), # more bottom space
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)), # separate labels
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# --- Plot 2: Time ---
p_time <- ggplot(
  plot_time,
  aes(x = group, y = response, color = ai, group = ai)
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = csu_ai_colors,
    breaks = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    labels = c(
      "Manual Coding",
      "AI-Assisted Coding"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Coding\nTime",
    x = "Group",
    y = "Predicted Time [sec]", #  restored
    color = "AI Use"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(10, 40, 12, 5), #  BIG right margin (fix clipping)
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 12)), #  push label outward
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)), #  prevent overlap
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# --- Combine with spacer (KEY FIX) ---
combined <- (p_beta | plot_spacer() | p_time) +
  plot_layout(
    widths = c(1.05, 0.06, 1.25), #  small gap between panels
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.1, "lines"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(0.4, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

combined

ggsave(
  "../plots/combined.png",
  plot = combined,
  # <-- increase this
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

Builds and saves a bar chart of manually entered GatorTron performance metrics and confidence intervals.

```{r plot-gatortron-metrics}
# Visualize externally supplied model-performance values; these values are hard-coded rather than calculated above.
gatortron_metrics_df <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Metric, ~Estimate, ~CI_half,
  "F1", 76.9, 0.14,
  "Precision", 81.5, 1.74,
  "Recall", 74.4, 1.14,
  "Exact Match", 52.2, 0.66
) %>%
  mutate(
    CI_low  = Estimate - CI_half,
    CI_high = Estimate + CI_half,
    Metric  = factor(Metric, levels = Metric)
  )

p_bar <- ggplot(gatortron_metrics_df, aes(x = Metric, y = Estimate, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Estimate)),
    vjust = -2.75,
    size = 5,
    color = "black",
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", CI_low, CI_high)),
    vjust = -2.0, size = 4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(50, 100, 10),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", x)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(50, 100), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = csu_palette_4) +
  labs(
    title = "GatorTron Model Performance",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Score"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

p_bar

ggsave(
  "../plots/metrics.png",
  plot = p_bar,
  # <-- increase this
  dpi = 300
)
```
